vsm2.20:43.1: And just as one who is comprehending the material should see the generation of the material,
vsm2.20:43.2: so too one who is comprehending the immaterial should see the generation of the immaterial.
vsm2.20:43.3: And that is through the eighty-one mundane arisings of consciousness,
vsm2.20:43.4: that is to say, it is by kamma accumulated in a previous becoming that this immaterial mentality is generated.
vsm2.20:43.5: And in the first place it is generated as one of the nineteen kinds of arisings of consciousness as rebirth-linking (XVII.130).
vsm2.20:43.6:
But the modes in which it is generated should be understood according to the method
given in the Description of the Dependent Origination (XVII.134f.).
vsm2.20:43.7:
That same nineteenfold arising of consciousness is generated as life-continuum as well,
starting from the consciousness next to rebirth-linking consciousness,
vsm2.20:43.8: and as death consciousness at the termination of the life span.
vsm2.20:43.9: And when it is of the sense sphere, and the object in the six doors is a vivid one, it is also generated as registration.
vsm2.20:44.1: In the course of an existence, because the eye is intact and because visible data have come into focus,
vsm2.20:44.2: eye-consciousness, together with its associated states, supported by light and caused by attention, is generated.
vsm2.20:44.3: For it is actually when a visible datum has reached presence
vsm2.20:44.4: that it impinges on the eye at the instant of the eye-sensitivity’s presence.
vsm2.20:44.5: When it has done so, the life-continuum arises and ceases twice.
vsm2.20:44.6: Next to arise is the functional mind element with that same object, accomplishing the function of adverting.
vsm2.20:44.7: Next to that, eye-consciousness, which is the result of profitable or of unprofitable kamma and sees that same visible datum.
vsm2.20:44.8: Next, the resultant mind element, which receives that same visible datum.
vsm2.20:44.9: Next, the resultant root-causeless mind-consciousness element, which investigates that same visible datum.
vsm2.20:44.10:
Next, the functional mind-consciousness element without root-cause and accompanied by equanimity,
which determines that same visible datum.
vsm2.20:44.11:
Next, it is generated either as one from among the profitable ((l)–(8)), unprofitable
((22)–(33)), or functional ((71) and (73)–(80)) kinds of consciousness belonging to the sense sphere,
either as consciousness accompanied by equanimity and without root-cause (71),
vsm2.20:44.12: or as five or seven impulsions.
vsm2.20:44.13: Next, in the case of sense-sphere beings, it is generated as any of the eleven kinds of registration consciousness
vsm2.20:44.14: conforming as to object with the impulsions.
vsm2.20:44.15: The same applies to the remaining doors.
vsm2.20:44.16: But in the case of the mind door-exalted consciousnesses also arise.
vsm2.20:44.17: This is how the generation of the immaterial should be seen in the case of the six doors.
vsm2.20:44.18: One who sees the generation of the immaterial thus is said to “comprehend the immaterial at another time” (§21).
vsm2.20:45.1: This is how one meditator accomplishes the development of understanding, progressing gradually
vsm2.20:45.2: by comprehending at one time the material and at another time the immaterial, by attributing the three characteristics to them.
vsm2.20:46.1:
Another comprehends formations by attributing the three characteristics to them through
the medium of the material septad and the immaterial septad.
vsm2.20:46.2:
Herein, one who comprehends them by attributing the characteristics in the following seven ways is said to comprehend by attributing
through the medium of the material septad, that is to say, (1) as taking up and putting down,
vsm2.20:46.3: (2) as disappearance of what grows old in each stage,
vsm2.20:46.9:
Hence the Ancients said:

> “(1) As taking up and putting down,
> (2) As growth and decline in every stage,
> (3) As nutriment, (4) as temperature,
> (5) As kamma, and (6) as consciousness,
> (7) As natural materiality—
> He sees with seven detailed insights.”
vsm2.20:47.3:
So the meditator allots one hundred years for this “taking up” and “putting down” and he
attributes the three characteristics to formations.
vsm2.20:47.4: How? All formations between these limits are impermanent.
vsm2.20:47.5:
Why? Because of the occurrence of rise and fall, because of change,
because of temporariness, and because of preclusion of permanence.
vsm2.20:47.6:
But since arisen formations have arrived at presence, and when present
are afflicted by ageing, and on arriving at ageing are bound to dissolve,
vsm2.20:47.7:
they are therefore painful because of continual oppression, because of being hard to bear,
because of being the basis of suffering, and because of precluding pleasure.
vsm2.20:47.8:
And since no one has any power over arisen formations in the three instances, “Let them not reach presence”,
“Let those that have reached presence not age,” and “Let those that have reached ageing not dissolve,”
vsm2.20:47.9:
and they are void of the possibility of any power being exercised over them, they are therefore not-self because void,
because ownerless, because unsusceptible to the wielding of power, and because of precluding a self.
vsm2.20:48.1:
Having attributed the three characteristics to materiality allotted one hundred years for the “taking up” and “putting
down” thus, he next attributes them according to disappearance of what grows old in each stage.
vsm2.20:48.2:
Herein, “disappearance of what grows old in each stage” is a name for the disappearance of the materiality
that has grown old during a stage of life.
vsm2.20:48.3: The meaning is that he attributes the three characteristics by means of that.
vsm2.20:49.1: How? He divides that same hundred years up into three stages, that is, the first stage, the middle stage, and the last stage.
vsm2.20:49.2: Herein, the first thirty-three years are called the first stage,
vsm2.20:49.3: the next thirty-four years are called the middle stage,
vsm2.20:49.4: and the next thirty-three years are called the last stage.
vsm2.20:49.5:
So after dividing it up into these three stages, he attributes the three characteristics thus: The materiality
occurring in the first stage ceased there without reaching the middle stage: therefore it is impermanent;
vsm2.20:49.6: what is impermanent is painful; what is painful is not-self.
vsm2.20:49.7:
Also the materiality occurring in the middle stage ceased there without reaching the last stage:
therefore it is impermanent too and painful and not-self.
vsm2.20:49.8:
Also there is no materiality occurring in the thirty-three years of the last stage
that is capable of out-lasting death: therefore that is impermanent too, painful, not-self.
vsm2.20:50.1:
Having attributed the three characteristics according to “disappearance of what grows old in each
stage” thus by means of the first stage, etc., he again attributes the three characteristics
according to “disappearance of what grows old in each stage” by means of the following ten decades:
vsm2.20:50.2: the tender decade, the sport decade, the beauty decade, the strength decade, the understanding decade,
vsm2.20:50.3: the decline decade, the stooping decade, the bent decade, the dotage decade, and the prone decade.
vsm2.20:51.1:
Herein, as to these decades: in the first place, the first ten years of a person with a hundred
years’ life are called the tender decade; for then he is a tender unsteady child.
vsm2.20:51.2: The next ten years are called the sport decade; for he is very fond of sport then.
vsm2.20:51.3: The next ten years are called the beauty decade; for his beauty reaches its full extent then.
vsm2.20:51.4: The next ten years are called the strength decade; for his strength and power reach their full extent then.
vsm2.20:51.5:
The next ten years are called the understanding decade; for his understanding is well established by then.
Even in one naturally weak in understanding some understanding, it seems, arises at that time.
vsm2.20:51.6:
The next ten years are called the decline decade; for his fondness for sport and his beauty,
strength, and understanding decline then.
vsm2.20:51.7: The next ten years are called the stooping decade; for his figure stoops forward then.
vsm2.20:51.8: The next ten years are called the bent decade; for his figure becomes bent like the end of a plough then.
vsm2.20:51.9: The next ten years are called the dotage decade; for he is doting then and forgets what he does.
vsm2.20:51.10: The next ten years are called the prone decade; for a centenarian mostly lies prone.
vsm2.20:52.1:
Herein, in order to attribute the three characteristics according to “disappearance of what grows
old in each stage” by means of these decades, the meditator considers thus:
vsm2.20:52.2:
The materiality occurring in the first decade ceases there without reaching the second decade:
therefore it is impermanent, painful, not-self.
vsm2.20:52.3:
The materiality occurring in the second decade … the materiality occurring in the ninth
decade ceases there without reaching the tenth decade;
vsm2.20:52.4:
the materiality occurring in the tenth decade ceases there without reaching the next becoming:
therefore it is impermanent, painful, not-self. That is how he attributes the three characteristics.
vsm2.20:53.1:
Having attributed the three characteristics according to “disappearance of what
grows old in each stage” thus by means of the decades,
vsm2.20:53.2:
he again attributes the three characteristics according to “disappearance of what grows old in each
stage” by taking that same hundred years in twenty parts of five years each.
vsm2.20:54.2:
The materiality occurring in the first five years ceases there without reaching the second
five years: therefore it is impermanent, painful, not-self.
vsm2.20:54.3:
The materiality occurring in the second five years … in the third … in the nineteenth
five years ceases there without reaching the twentieth five years.
vsm2.20:54.4:
There is no materiality occurring in the twentieth five years that is capable of outlasting death;
therefore that is impermanent too, painful, not-self.
vsm2.20:55.1:
Having attributed the three characteristics according to “disappearance of what grows
old in each stage” thus by means of the twenty parts,
vsm2.20:55.2:
he again attributes the three characteristics according to “disappearance of what grows
old in each stage” by taking twenty-five parts of four years each.
vsm2.20:55.3: Next, by taking thirty-three parts of three years each,
vsm2.20:55.4: by taking fifty parts of two years each,
vsm2.20:55.5: by taking a hundred parts of one year each.
vsm2.20:55.6:
Next he attributes the three characteristics according to “disappearance of what grows old in each
stage” by means of each of the three seasons, taking each year in three parts.
vsm2.20:56.1: How? The materiality occurring in the four months of the rains (vassāna) ceases there without reaching the winter (hemanta).
vsm2.20:56.2: The materiality occurring in the winter ceases there without reaching the summer (gimha).
vsm2.20:56.3:
The materiality occurring in the summer ceases there without reaching the rains again:
therefore it is impermanent, painful, not-self.
vsm2.20:57.1:
Having attributed them thus, he again takes one year in six parts and attributes the three characteristics to this
materiality according to “disappearance of what grows old in each stage” thus:
vsm2.20:57.2: The materiality occurring in the two months of the rains (vassāna) ceases there without reaching the autumn (sarada).
vsm2.20:57.3: The materiality occurring in the autumn … in the winter (hemanta) … in the cool (sisira) … in the spring (vasanta) …
vsm2.20:57.4:
the materiality occurring in the summer (gimha) ceases there without reaching the rains again:
therefore it is impermanent too, painful, not-self.
vsm2.20:58.1: Having attributed them thus, he next attributes the characteristics by means of the dark and bright halves of the moon thus:
vsm2.20:58.2: The materiality occurring in the dark half of the moon ceases there without reaching the bright half;
vsm2.20:58.3:
the materiality occurring in the bright half ceases there without reaching the dark half:
therefore it is impermanent, painful, not-self.
vsm2.20:59.1: Next he attributes the three characteristics by means of night and day thus:
vsm2.20:59.2: The materiality occurring in the night ceases there without reaching the day;
vsm2.20:59.3: the materiality occurring in the day ceases there without reaching the night: therefore it is impermanent, painful, not-self.
vsm2.20:60.1: Next he attributes the three characteristics by taking that same day in six parts beginning with the morning thus:
vsm2.20:60.2: The materiality occurring in the morning ceased there without reaching the noon;
vsm2.20:60.3: the materiality occurring in the noon … without reaching the evening;
vsm2.20:60.4: the materiality occurring in the evening … the first watch;
vsm2.20:60.5: the materiality occurring in the first watch … the middle watch;
vsm2.20:60.6: the materiality occurring in the middle watch ceased there without reaching the last watch;
vsm2.20:60.7:
the materiality occurring in the last watch ceased there without reaching the morning again:
therefore it is impermanent, painful, not-self.
